_provenance: Copied from UI_v2:code/Model1/model_bundle.pkl (WBP-train.py), retrained under scikit-learn 1.8.0 to match this repo's pinned version (source pkl was trained under an unpinned >=1.3.0 env). Superseded the previous GradientBoostingClassifier bundle (burnout_gbm_model.pkl, 135 features) from the preprocessor branch. See ../docs/ML_MODELS_OVERVIEW.md for the full writeup.
note_on_output: This model regresses a continuous 0-100 burnout_risk_computed score, unlike the previous model which was a 4-class classifier with predict_proba. The continuous score is bucketed into 3 classes (not 4 — 'Critical' no longer exists) via percentile thresholds computed on the full training set. predicted_probabilities in the API response is therefore a one-hot vector on the bucketed class, not a calibrated probability distribution — see modules/ml/predict.py.

engineered_features.workload_compatibility_score: computed live from employees.weekly_capacity_hours/current_project_count, same formula as training's WBP-pp.py but WITHOUT the Gaussian noise term training added for synthetic-data realism (inappropriate for deterministic live inference)
engineered_features.availability_score: computed live from employees.is_available/current_project_count, same bucketed formula as training's WBP-pp.py, noise term omitted for the same reason

all_features_live: Unlike the previous burnout model, every one of these 17 features is sourceable from the live DB (employees + latest burnout_indicators row per employee) — no ADD COLUMN/backfill gap.
imputation: This model has no built-in imputer (unlike the old Pipeline([SimpleImputer, ...])). Missing raw inputs (e.g. no burnout_indicators row yet for a new employee) are filled with the training-set median before scoring — see live_medians below, sourced from UI_v2:code/Model1/processed.csv.

metrics.note: Re-measured by re-running WBP-train.py against UI_v2:code/Model1/processed.csv under scikit-learn 1.8.0 (this branch's pinned version) — not persisted anywhere in the source repo originally.
